questions.title: Pig Latin Word Encoder
questions.description:
A language toy converts each word of a sentence into Pig Latin by moving the first letter to the end and adding "ay". The output preserves lowercased words and word boundaries. Implement the converter character by character without using regex substitution methods.

Input Format:
A single line containing one or more words separated by single spaces.

Output Format:
The Pig Latin encoded line (each word's first letter moved to end and "ay" appended, all lowercased).

Constraints:
1 <= line length <= 200
questions.sourcecode:
def pig(word)
  return word if word.length < 1
  w = word.downcase
  first = w[0]
  rest = w[1..]
  rest + first + "ay"
end

line = gets.chomp
words = []
cur = ""
line.each_char do |c|
  if c == " "
    words << pig(cur) unless cur.empty?
    cur = ""
  else
    cur += c
  end
end
words << pig(cur) unless cur.empty?
puts words.join(" ")

questions.title: Palindrome Sentence Verifier
questions.description:
A palindrome checker must decide whether a sentence reads the same forwards and backwards after ignoring spaces, punctuation and letter case. Implement the verifier by iterating characters manually rather than using regex substitution or reverse.

Input Format:
A single line containing a sentence (letters, digits, spaces, punctuation).

Output Format:
The string "true" if the cleaned sentence is a palindrome, otherwise "false".

Constraints:
1 <= sentence length <= 200
questions.sampleinput2: A man a plan a canal Panama
questions.sourcecode:
def cleaned(line)
  out = ""
  line.each_char do |c|
    if (c >= "a" && c <= "z") || (c >= "A" && c <= "Z") || (c >= "0" && c <= "9")
      out += c.downcase
    end
  end
  out
end

line = gets.chomp
s = cleaned(line)
n = s.length
ok = true
i = 0
while i < n / 2
  if s[i] != s[n - 1 - i]
    ok = false
    break
  end
  i += 1
end
puts ok ? "true" : "false"

questions.title: CamelCase to snake_case Converter
questions.description:
A code style tool rewrites CamelCase identifiers into snake_case. Each uppercase letter becomes lowercase and is prefixed with an underscore, except when it is the very first character. Implement the conversion character by character without regex substitution.

Input Format:
A single line containing a CamelCase identifier.

Output Format:
The snake_case form of the identifier.

Constraints:
1 <= identifier length <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
def to_snake(s)
  out = ""
  s.each_char do |c|
    if c >= "A" && c <= "Z"
      out += "_"
      out += c.downcase
    else
      out += c
    end
  end
  out = out[1..] if out[0] == "_"
  out
end

line = gets.chomp
puts to_snake(line)

questions.title: CSV Field Extractor
questions.description:
A tiny CSV parser reads one row and a column index, then prints the value at that column. Implement the field splitting by iterating characters manually rather than using the built-in split method or the CSV library.

Input Format:
Line 1: a comma separated row of fields (no quoted fields).
Line 2: a zero-based column index.

Output Format:
The value of the field at the requested column index.

Constraints:
1 <= row length <= 200; 0 <= index < number of fields
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= row length <= 200; 0 <= index < number of fields
questions.sourcecode:
def field_at(line, index)
  fields = []
  cur = ""
  line.each_char do |c|
    if c == ","
      fields << cur
      cur = ""
    else
      cur += c
    end
  end
  fields << cur
  fields[index]
end

line = gets.chomp
index = gets.to_i
puts field_at(line, index)

questions.title: ASCII Byte Average Calculator
questions.description:
An encoding inspector computes the average ASCII code of the characters in a string. Read a line and print the integer average (rounded down via integer division) without using String#bytes or aggregation methods like sum/inject.

Input Format:
A single line of text.

Output Format:
An integer — the floor of the average ASCII code of the characters.

Constraints:
1 <= line length <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
def byte_average(line)
  total = 0
  count = 0
  line.each_char do |c|
    total += c.ord
    count += 1
  end
  count == 0 ? 0 : total / count
end

line = gets.chomp
puts byte_average(line)

questions.title: Caesar Cipher Encoder
questions.description:
A Caesar cipher encoder shifts each letter by k positions (preserving case and wrapping around the alphabet) while leaving non-letter characters unchanged. Implement the shift using each_char with ord/chr arithmetic; do not use gsub, sub or tr.

Input Format:
Line 1: the text to encode.
Line 2: a non-negative integer shift k.

Output Format:
The encoded text.

Constraints:
1 <= text length <= 200; 0 <= k <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
def shift(c, k)
  if c >= "a" && c <= "z"
    base = "a".ord
    n = c.ord - base
    n = (n + k) % 26
    (base + n).chr
  elsif c >= "A" && c <= "Z"
    base = "A".ord
    n = c.ord - base
    n = (n + k) % 26
    (base + n).chr
  else
    c
  end
end

line = gets.chomp
k = gets.to_i
result = ""
line.each_char { |c| result += shift(c, k) }
puts result

questions.title: Title Case Article Generator
questions.description:
An article formatter converts a headline so the first letter of every word is uppercase and the remaining letters are lowercase, preserving the original spacing. Implement the conversion by iterating characters; do not use String#capitalize or gsub.

Input Format:
A single line containing a headline.

Output Format:
The title-cased headline.

Constraints:
1 <= headline length <= 200
questions.sourcecode:
def title_case(line)
  result = ""
  new_word = true
  line.each_char do |c|
    if c == " "
      result += c
      new_word = true
    elsif new_word
      result += c.upcase
      new_word = false
    else
      result += c.downcase
    end
  end
  result
end

line = gets.chomp
puts title_case(line)

questions.title: Masked Email Printer
questions.description:
A privacy tool masks the local part of an email address so only its first character is visible, followed by three asterisks and the domain. Implement the masking by scanning characters manually with a while loop; do not use regex substitution methods.

Input Format:
A single line containing an email address.

Output Format:
The masked email: first character + "***" + the part starting at the @ sign (including @).

Constraints:
1 <= email length <= 100; email always contains exactly one @ character
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= email length <= 100; email contains exactly one @
questions.sourcecode:
def mask_email(email)
  at_pos = -1
  i = 0
  while i < email.length
    if email[i] == "@"
      at_pos = i
      break
    end
    i += 1
  end
  return email if at_pos == -1
  first = email[0]
  domain = email[at_pos..]
  first + "***" + domain
end

line = gets.chomp
puts mask_email(line)

questions.title: Word Frequency Reporter
questions.description:
A word analytics tool reads a sentence and prints each distinct word (lowercased) together with how many times it occurs, sorted by count descending then alphabetically ascending. Implement counting manually with a hash; do not use tally, group_by, count or inject.

Input Format:
A single line containing words separated by single spaces.

Output Format:
One line per distinct word in the form "<word> <count>", sorted as described.

Constraints:
1 <= line length <= 500
questions.sampleinput1: the cat the dog the bird
questions.sourcecode:
def gather_words(line)
  counts = {}
  word = ""
  line.each_char do |c|
    if c == " "
      unless word.empty?
        counts[word] = (counts[word] || 0) + 1
        word = ""
      end
    else
      word += c.downcase
    end
  end
  unless word.empty?
    counts[word] = (counts[word] || 0) + 1
  end
  counts
end

line = gets.chomp
counts = gather_words(line)
result = counts.map { |k, v| [k, v] }.sort do |a, b|
  if a[1] == b[1]
    a[0] <=> b[0]
  else
    b[1] <=> a[1]
  end
end
result.each do |w, n|
  puts "#{w} #{n}"
end
